decisive_items: Reversible Effect on Cystoid Macular Edema (CME) Secondary to Retinal Vein Occlusion After Stopping Niacin Therapy
persistent central macular thickness of 669.8 [79.3] μm
severe macular changes with associated edema
response.rationale: The figure title explicitly identifies CME secondary to retinal vein occlusion, with niacin therapy as a modifying factor. Imaging findings (persistent central macular thickness, edema) align with CME/RVO. R2 labels the drug etiology but is subordinate to the primary diagnosis of CME secondary to RVO.

rejected.why: Niacin is a contributing factor, not the primary diagnosis; the figure title clearly states the underlying condition is CME secondary to retinal vein occlusion.
